prompt: Put these stages of a typical agency software project in the order they usually happen, first at the top.

task.prompt: Put these stages of a typical agency software project in the order they usually happen, first at the top.

items.label: QA testing and user acceptance testing (UAT)
UI/UX design and clickable prototype sign-off

task.explanation: Requirements come first, designs are approved before heavy build, sprints produce testable work, QA and UAT gate the launch, and support follows release.

prompt: A new BD rep wrote this explanation of the delivery process for a prospect. Mark the sentences that would set wrong expectations.

task.prompt: A new BD rep wrote this explanation of the delivery process for a prospect. Mark the sentences that would set wrong expectations.

segments.text: We work in two-week sprints, and you will see a demo of working features at the end of each one.
Once development starts, you can add any new feature at no extra cost or time.
segments.issue: Scope changes go through a change request; they affect cost or timeline.

segments.text: A project manager is your single point of contact for day-to-day questions.
QA is optional, so we usually skip it to launch faster.
segments.issue: QA is a standard part of delivery; skipping it shifts bugs onto the client's users.

segments.text: Before launch you will test the app yourself in a staging environment (UAT).
After launch there is a warranty period for bugs, and maintenance can be covered by a separate plan.

prompt: A first-time founder on a call asks: "What happens after I sign? I've never built software before."

task.prompt: A first-time founder on a call asks: "What happens after I sign? I've never built software before."

steps.question: What is the best first thing to explain?
options: That the app will be live within a week of signing
That we start with discovery to confirm scope and priorities before design and build
That they do not need to be involved until launch
The exact programming languages the developers will use
steps.explanation: Non-technical founders need the shape of the process; discovery is the first step and sets expectations.

steps.question: The founder asks how they will know the project is on track. What do you say?
options: We send a final report when the contract ends
They will see everything at launch
Sprint demos every couple of weeks and a shared board showing progress
They can email the developers directly whenever they like
steps.explanation: Regular demos and a visible backlog give the client real evidence of progress.

prompt: A client wants a launch date. The backlog is estimated at 180 story points, the team completes about 30 points per two-week sprint, and the plan adds one extra sprint at the end for QA hardening and UAT. How many sprints, and how many weeks, until launch?

task.prompt: A client wants a launch date. The backlog is estimated at 180 story points, the team completes about 30 points per two-week sprint, and the plan adds one extra sprint at the end for QA hardening and UAT. How many sprints, and how many weeks, until launch?
task.explanation: 180 / 30 = 6 build sprints, plus 1 hardening sprint = 7 sprints; 7 x 2 weeks = 14 weeks.

prompt: Mid-project, a client emails BD directly: "Can you add a loyalty-points feature? It's small, should be quick." The signed scope does not include it.

task.prompt: Mid-project, a client emails BD directly: "Can you add a loyalty-points feature? It's small, should be quick." The signed scope does not include it.

steps.question: What should BD do first?
options: Tell the client new features are impossible once a project starts
Ask a developer privately to squeeze it in
Loop in the project manager and treat it as a change request to be estimated
Promise it will be done this sprint to keep the client happy
steps.explanation: Change requests are estimated by delivery and agreed in writing; BD should not commit on delivery's behalf.

steps.question: The estimate comes back at one extra sprint. What is the best way to present it?
options: Hide the cost inside the next invoice
Only offer to add it at full cost with no alternatives
Offer options: add a sprint and cost, swap it for an equal-sized item, or schedule it for phase 2
Drop the request quietly
steps.explanation: Trade-off options keep the client in control of scope, budget and timeline.

prompt: A bug is found in production after launch. Rank these responses from most to least appropriate.

task.prompt: A bug is found in production after launch. Rank these responses from most to least appropriate.

items.label: Tell the client it passed UAT so it is their responsibility
Ignore it until the client complains a second time
Log it, have QA reproduce it, assess severity, and fix under the warranty or maintenance plan
Ask the client for steps to reproduce, then fix it whenever the team is free

task.explanation: A structured triage under the agreed support terms is best; vague timing is weaker; blaming UAT damages trust; ignoring it is worst.

prompt: What is UAT in a software project?

options: The agency's internal code review
A security audit done after launch
The client testing the finished features in a staging environment before launch
Automated tests developers write for each function
mcq.explanation: User acceptance testing is the client confirming the software does what they need before it goes live.

prompt: Why do agencies demo working software at the end of each sprint?

options: To replace QA testing
So the client can approve the final design for the first time
So the client sees real progress and can give feedback early
Because contracts require a demo before every invoice in all countries
mcq.explanation: Frequent demos surface misunderstandings while they are cheap to fix and build client trust.

prompt: A client asks why the quote includes a separate maintenance plan after the warranty. What is the best explanation?

options: Apps never need changes after launch, so maintenance is optional padding
Warranty covers defects in what was delivered; maintenance covers OS and library updates, monitoring and small changes over time
Maintenance is only needed if the code was written badly
Warranty and maintenance are the same thing billed twice
mcq.explanation: Software keeps changing around the app (OS releases, dependency and security updates), which is ongoing work beyond fixing original defects.

prompt: Which explanation of agile is most useful for a non-technical buyer?

options: Agile guarantees the project finishes early
We build in short cycles, show you working features often, and re-prioritise the remaining work with you as we learn
Agile means there is no plan or fixed scope
Agile means the developers decide what to build
mcq.explanation: Agile is short iterations with frequent feedback and reprioritisation, not the absence of a plan.
